summary: Absorbed bench pin cbe3bf9's portable-core redesign into the env repository as one atomic change set. The pin's deletion of the embedded platform (benchmark/platform/riscv64-nemu-linux) and its move of the CHERI/Morello build skips into the tracked registry obsoleted the env's Python registry derivation (derive_registry.py) and its reimplementation of corpus keying (build_corpus.sh); the submodule worktree had already moved to the new commit, leaving every deploy preflight red. The cycle landed: the pin bump as env.sh text plus the submodule gitlink in one commit; a single staging orchestrator, scripts/common/stage_corpus.sh, which copies the bench tree into a per-lane scratch tree and drives the pinned runner's corpus mode (run-test corpus make-only exhausted-run) with the environment scrubbed so the runner owns keying and skip handling; scripts/common/corpus_manifest.py, a skip-aware verifier adapted from the venue's own that checks the staged set against the tracked registry (units minus records whose skip names the lane token), re-measures its path-length budget against keyed names, and writes the new-schema manifest (units, side_files, support_files, skipped with reasons; expected_failures is gone); the NEMU venue package absorbed from the dead platform path into scripts/riscv64_nemu/venue/ (image builder, boot driver, guest overlay) with the runset mechanism deleted everywhere and the unique build-corpus steps (cross-built guest scheduler, NEEDED plus PT_INTERP library closure, the guest-truth sys_info prefix for results.dat) moved into the absorbed image builder; every guest runner converged on run-test no-make corpus exhausted-run; and all seven executable lanes re-stamped at the pin, record-for-record equal to their 2026-10-27 baselines (riscv64 and riscv64-nemu each 225 clean, 21 declared) with compare_lanes.py exiting 0. Key gotchas: the one plain-name consumer (acc-check-ASLR's system() call) is kept alive by a declared support file in the staged tree; MAKEFLAGS leakage of the lane ARCH is scrubbed before the corpus invocation; the host runner is rebuilt with make -B in a scrubbed env and readelf-asserted as a host ELF. Verified end-to-end by a 12/12 tester round including byte-identical double rebuilds of the absorbed image builder; CHERI guest boots remain deferred bring-up with their staging legs proven. Two issues found and resolved in-cycle (a Step 3/Step 4 enable-flag wording contradiction; stale Makefile venue comments); one bench-side observation recorded (a stale cheri skip row owned by the bench-internal cycle).

Unified the bench pin at f9e4ba7 across the seven executable lanes and delivered the first cross-lane comparison at a single pin. The pin bump carries the bench's aarch64 result-class declarations (the HWASan/MTE producer set and the PAuth crash codes, so designed behaviour no longer reads out-of-expect) and the NEMU venue's staging rebuild (scratch-tree corpus build, reproducible image, publish-on-success manifest), which let every env text and diagnostic that described the old registry swap be rewritten to the scratch-tree invariants: submodule HEAD equals the pin, tree clean, dirt is a real edit, and every git read is rc-guarded. Provenance hardening: version_stamp records bench-head, bench-tree and run-status in every stamp, and all collectors pass their final rc. Guard hardening: the aarch64 and shared-corpus paths assert the submodule pin, prepare.sh cross-checks its smoke class flags against the pinned benchmark Makefile (failing closed), the host-lane collectors treat results.json and results.dat as required and parseable, the aarch64 run recipe holds the lane lock across both legs through a verified LANE_LOCK_INHERITED marker with fd 9 closed for children, and every lane script opens the lock append-style so a contender preserves the holder name. The committed comparison tool scripts/common/compare_lanes.py classifies the seven lanes against the git-pinned registry (git show pin:configure.json) with a closed verdict vocabulary, a three-valued exit contract, a class-masked carve-out scoped to the mte lane's HWASan producer, and versions.txt-based stamp selection that keeps retirement directories inert. The seven-lane re-stamp exposed two real findings, both fixed in-cycle: the pa calibration cascade is dead (offsets stored, declared crash code delivered) and the bti lane's build class SIGILLed on a PAuth-less default CPU because the bench's new STRIP_PAC compiles to xpaci under armv8.5 — fixed env-side with a QEMU_CPU=max request plus a non-vacuous deploy smoke whose opcode census cannot pass vacuously. Final state: 178 verification checks green, the plan's literal default-selection gate command exits 0 with empty findings, the CHERI pair keeps its previous-pin stamps excluded by design, and the durable STRIP_PAC runtime-capability gating remains a named bench-side follow-up.

The four aarch64-family lanes had never executed a test case: env.sh exported QEMU_VERSION, which this venue's qemu-user reads itself, printing its version banner and exiting 0 for any value before -cpu parsing and before loading a guest, so 21 stamps from 2026-10-13 to 2026-10-24 are non-execution records. The cycle renamed the pin to QEMU_PIN_VERSION and dropped it from the exports, made the deploy smoke assert the guest loader's own content instead of an exit code, and added lane-representative execution legs: a PAC-ret probe for pa, an -fsanitize=hwaddress program for mte under a ratified two-outcome acceptance (the runtime's LeakSanitizer leg cannot run under qemu-user), and deliberately none for bti because BTI hints execute as NOPs. It pinned QEMU_CPU_AARCH64_MTE and the new QEMU_CPU_AARCH64_PA to max, the venue default plus PAuth, which is load-bearing for the pa lane's retaa epilogue; sys_info records the CPU request and the observation separately; and the request path is hardened, with the request-less lanes clearing an ambient QEMU_CPU, both scripts dropping an inherited QEMU_VERSION, run.sh's collector folding a collection rc into the exit status, and its submodule gate distinguishing a failing git from a dirty tree. The family was re-stamped at the bumped bench pin 47d6f9d, where the pa lane's 226-record SIGILL class is gone and the mte lane carries the HWASan-99 class; a post-implementation mega-audit (0 High, 19 Medium, 27 Low) and the Phase 6 reviewer (0 Critical, 3 Warning) drove a hardening round, with two code-level warnings deferred as standalone markers. The pin bump re-bases only the aarch64 family; the riscv64 and CHERI re-stamp is a named successor.

Unified the environment's benchmark pin and produced the cross-lane comparison the lane set exists for: every lane's newest stamp had sat at a different bench commit (x86_64 at c2c7039, riscv64 and aarch64-morello at c8c6000, the four aarch64 lanes and cheri_riscv64 at 74195c4, riscv64-nemu at a09f570), so no honest cross-platform comparison existed and the bench's new return-code contract — every case's process status a declared, meaning-carrying value, with the F2/267 defect fixed at the source — was unconfirmed on real lanes. The cycle bumped env.sh's BENCH_COMMIT to f4c916a821a6f3fa7024a75b1a25304ae4555729 and re-ran all nine lane configurations at that one pin, one at a time under the shared lane lock, retiring the repo's two pending cross-repo envelopes and folding the pycache ignore fix along the way. Classification of every stamp against the registry's documented meanings produced the headline deliverable, the cross-lane comparison snapshot: per-category zero/declared/out-of-expect tables across acc, cfi, cpi, mss and mts, plus every divergence from the x86_64 reference traced to a named record with both codes and their declared meanings; the two riscv64 venues (the qemu guest and the NEMU venue) agree with each other record for record and diverge from x86_64 in the same eight records. The user's intent check, executed against the deployed corpora with no lane re-run, showed the four undeclared statuses to be case-delivery defects rather than missing declarations: 214 and 50 are one defect in which the compiler-generated landing block lost its exit argument so the status is the label address's low byte, 262 is a mis-aimed return-address write caught by main's stack canary, and cheri_riscv64's declared cfi-return-without-call value of 1 is vacuous because the lane records no frame-size; a structural scan over the sixteen-source label-address family found exactly that one genuine delivery defect. Dispositions were user-decided: two fix-first items delivered to the bench tracker as the cfi delivery defects and the F2 re-open, the aarch64-mte lane's unbacked MTE claim deferred to a new environment cycle as a standalone deferral (the pin is rejected by this host's qemu-aarch64 while the variant's 246 verdicts equal the plain lane's, record for record), the Morello 260 held for one guest-side observation before any declaration, and the docs re-marked against the new stamps — README's pins table now a single uniform row, an honest aarch64-mte caveat naming the missing evidence, and .claude ignored wholesale in .gitignore and CLAUDE.md.

Added riscv64-nemu as a first-class lane of the cpu-sec-test-env dispatcher, wrapping the bench's own NEMU venue (benchmark/platform/riscv64-nemu-linux/) in the standard lane contract: the shared advisory lane lock, the results/<lane>/<stamp>/ stamp, env.sh pins, and the family publish policy — a timeout publishes nothing, every other failure publishes console evidence, and a completeness gate compares the run's record set against the deployed runset's derived registry before any result file is copied. The design is a thin wrapper: env.sh owns the pins (a bench-pin bump plus a relative-default NEMU_DIR/NEMU_BIN pair guarded by a hard NEMU_COMMIT), the Makefile dispatches deploy/run/clean and refuses dump because the corpus is staged corpus-keyed, and scripts/riscv64_nemu's prepare.sh and run.sh drive the platform's own build-corpus.sh, build-image.sh and run.sh with OUT under build/. Key mechanics: both platform legs run as their own sessions with the lane-lock fd closed and a session-wide kill (a sid == LEG_PID sweep with SIGKILL for survivors) on the TERM/INT trap and the watchdog-124 path, because the platform re-groups internally via its inner timeout NEMU; results are parsed from guest console markers rather than a shared filesystem, so boot.log is part of every non-timeout stamp, falling back to the lane's own platform log; and provenance carries the pins plus a nemu section (path, commit, describe --always --dirty, binary sha256) alongside the run and deploy metas, whose image and NEMU shas are cross-checked at publish. Trade-offs and gotchas: the venue image is not byte-reproducible (bench-side cpio without --reproducible), so stamps compare within one image; the guest-side results.dat records a dirty bench tree even at a clean pin (a bench-side staging artifact — the metas are authoritative); and the deploy consumes the platform's transient registry swap over the tracked configure.json, a documented exception to the benchmark read-only rule.

Resolved the initialize-claudemd-and-doc deferral by giving cpu-sec-test-env its first tracked root CLAUDE.md and an HTML documentation tree. On the user's explicit decisions the repo became public about Claude tooling via a bench-style CLAUDE.md, the README plus archived-plans surface was kept, and a new three-page doc tree with a shared stylesheet was added and made subject to the committed doc-structure gate. CLAUDE.md carries the lane-dispatch rules, the make commands, architecture notes, a Documentation index, and four Update-and-Commit hooks covering pin sync, lane and target sync, a pre-commit submodule-at-pin check, and the deferral norm. The doc tree documents the dispatcher internals — the lane lock, the env.sh pin doctrine, the derived registry, the opcode-extraction shim, provenance and the trust boundary — and the per-lane reference with execution paths, boot mechanics and prerequisites. Verification: two step scripts proven red then green, and the committed doc-structure checker passing with per-file evidence; the Phase 6 reviewer's six factual-accuracy warnings were all fixed before the commit.

This cycle supplied the CHERI-capable objdump the cheri_riscv64 lane needed and fixed the aarch64 lanes' shim PATH entry, then re-ran the five affected lanes at a bench pin carrying the extraction platform fix. scripts/common/build_corpus.sh gained a find_sdk_objdump helper mirroring find_sdk_clang, and the cheri case now passes the CTSRD SDK's riscv64cheri-objdump as OBJDUMP, with llvm-objdump as the fallback candidate, while pointing the lane's shim at the same absolute tool through scripts/common/shim.sh's extended argument contract, which accepts either a bare prefix or an absolute tool path. The aarch64 defect's root cause was that scripts/aarch64/run.sh prepended a repo-relative shim directory to PATH and then ran the scheduler after cd-ing into the benchmark submodule, so the entry stopped resolving and bare objdump fell through to the host disassembler; the directory is now root-anchored and two audit lines after the PATH export record the extraction tool and the bare-objdump resolution into each lane log, with a knob-derived objdump line added to the aarch64 sys_info.txt header. env.sh's BENCH_COMMIT moved from c8c6000 to 74195c4378e3cd97a7677555d66e473f19370962, the bench commit whose extractors require the published OBJDUMP knob; the five re-run lanes — cheri_riscv64 plus the four aarch64 variants — each published a 246-record stamp with acc-read-func 0 on the aarch64 lanes and the declared 290 on cheri, while riscv64 and aarch64-morello were not re-run and their stamps remain at the previous pin. Three deferrals — the cross-repo cheri objdump request and the two env-filed extraction defects — are resolved and retired, and the Phase 6 reviewer found no Critical or Warning findings.

Moved the environment's bench pin from the drop-cycle commit to the sweep commit c8c6000 — the continue-path fix, the catalog-guard hardening, the anchored opcode-extraction fix, five independent-assembly size directives and the confirmed expect-results registry diff — and re-ran all seven lanes one at a time for real-lane evidence, because the sweep's lane-visible changes had never executed on any lane. Six lanes produced 246-record stamps whose verdicts all fall into three classes — conforming, declared in the derived registry, or the known pre-existing handoff set — the sweep's extraction fix is lane-confirmed with riscv64 acc-read-func moving from 1 to 0 and mss-write-by-stack-pointer's 1 now declared, and aarch64-morello's verdicts are byte-identical to the old pin. Two bench-side defects in the opcode-extraction path surfaced by the confirmation and are deferred rather than worked around: cheri_riscv64 cannot deploy because the extractor selection has no CHERI variant, so the x64 fallback script meets an xcheri binary through a plain riscv64 objdump, and the four aarch64 host lanes cannot build acc-read-func because the same bare objdump call resolved to an aarch64-incapable binary, recorded as scheduler code 1025 failed-to-build. The analysis proved the old pin's aarch64 pass had been accidental — a two-symbol match fed objdump a mangled address and the fallback to address zero happened to capture the right bytes — and that the sweep's new hard error is what made the latent breakage visible, so a green extraction now means a real one. The recommended next move, recorded for the research, is to route the extraction through the bench's published OBJDUMP knob and give cheri_riscv64 its extractor values, then re-bump the pin and re-run only the two affected lane groups while the other five stamps stand.

Removed the environment-side workarounds that kept cpu-sec-bench's independent-assembly records on every non-x86 lane: env.sh now pins the bench commit carrying the assembly_return_site translation and the complete enable_riscv64_cheri target and ASMFLAGS block, the submodule is checked out at that commit, derive_registry.py no longer declares a wildcard skip or expected failures, and the six disable_independent_assembly build sites plus the two tolerant bring-up corpus invocations are gone. The two CHERI prepare scripts now build and stage the strict corpus and gained the same EXIT cleanup trap as the riscv64 lane builder, so a failed prepare cannot leave the shared benchmark worktree dirty; the retained bring-up capability stays available as a documented tool. Acceptance ran seven lanes one at a time (riscv64, plain aarch64, the pa/bti/mte variants, cheri_riscv64, aarch64-morello): every lane published a 246-record stamp, both asmfunc records executed on all of them, the strict corpora staged 145, 143 and 144 units with no expected failures, and the CHERI-only per-lane build-failure skips remain declared. One new bench-side defect surfaced and is handed to the sweep as a cross-repo deferral: the opcode-extraction scripts match the translated assembly_helper symbol with an unanchored grep, leaving riscv64 acc-read-func with an empty side file; all other verdict deviations are unchanged pre-existing expectations.

This plan replaced the probe-only CHERI scaffolds with two executable lanes that run the full cpu-sec-bench corpus: cheri_riscv64 boots a pinned purecap CheriBSD 15.0-CURRENT disk image under qemu-system-riscv64xcheri with the BBL firmware and an external kernel, and aarch64-morello boots the same class of image under qemu-system-morello through UEFI loader, both with the corpus delivered over two virtio-9p shares so no benchmark payload is baked into the images. All pins live in env.sh, sources are staged through checked-out git trees because cheribuild refuses non-git inputs, the CHERI-LLVM and Morello-LLVM SDKs and sysroots are pinned, and the shared corpus builder gained a tolerant bring-up mode plus a deploy-time derived registry whose per-lane skip table declares the recorded corpus build failures as 1025 skips while keeping the riscv64 derived output byte-identical. A host-side console driver logs into the guest over the serial pty and synchronises on bare-line echo tokens with a prompt-gated send, no re-send, a 2700-second deadline and a 3600-second cap, after live acceptance runs exposed a bare-timer re-send and then a prompt ordering race; the same runs caught the clang driver-mode defect caused by resolving the clang++ symlink and the missing Morello target triple. Acceptance is end-to-end: both lanes produce 246-record result sets with run-test-exit zero, exactly four and three 1025 skips, fully built manifests, and an independent tester classification with empty build-failure and leftover buckets; the remaining twenty-five outside-expect-results verdicts are candidate CHERI semantics owned by the bench-side successor.

This plan rebuilt cpu-sec-test-env as a single repository that builds and runs the cpu-sec-bench security benchmark on every supported architecture: an x86_64 native reference lane, an aarch64 lane that executes the host-built corpus through the kernel's binfmt_misc handler under qemu-aarch64 with pointer-authentication, branch-target-identification and memory-tagging variants, a riscv64 system lane that boots a Linux 6.18.56 guest built from pinned sources under qemu-system-riscv64 with results extracted over a virtio-9p share, and a CHERI dialect probe against freshly built CHERI-LLVM and Morello-LLVM toolchains. The design keeps every pin in env.sh as the single source of truth, derives the bench registry at deploy time so per-lane expected failures are declared rather than hard-coded, and enforces one-lane-at-a-time access through an advisory lock on build/.lane.lock because the benchmark submodule is a single mutable workdir consumed read-only at a pinned commit. The riscv64 image is byte-reproducible: identity pins for the kernel build, normalized mtimes, LC_ALL=C ordering, and cpio --reproducible so inode numbers stay out of the newc headers, a defect the tester found and the plan fixed and re-verified across three independent clean deploys. The lane scripts live under scripts/common, scripts/aarch64, scripts/riscv64 and scripts/cheri, orchestrated by the Makefile lane dispatcher, with the derived registry and corpus builder shared in scripts/common. Trade-offs and gotchas: the riscv64 CPU model must be rva23s64 because the distro cross toolchain tags every executable RVA64-profile RVA23U64, the guest kernel must default-enable userspace vector, the CHERI lanes are deliberately probe-only with full bring-up deferred, and two CFI records are skipped on riscv64 because the bench's independent-assembly source still carries an untranslated x86 return site.
